review.strongest_remaining_confound: The completeness baseline is only a weak three-feature trace-summary control, so the claimed residual may still be absorbed by other generic trace-composition/action-distribution features rather than surface-specific diagnostic information loss. At n<=18 probes, the frozen residual gate is also statistically fragile and may be driven by one or two probes.
review.required_change: Before implementation, strengthen the reduction control by adding a frozen generic full-trace-composition baseline using the non-fault-specific action-distribution features already available (for example take/move/examine/look/use fractions plus step/invalid/repeat fractions), and require the residual to survive beyond that baseline as well as the current three-feature completeness baseline. Also predefine a probe-level uncertainty/robustness check for the n<=18 gate, such as leave-one-probe-out sensitivity or exact paired resampling, without tuning thresholds after outcomes.
implementation_invariants: Keep prompt/workflow/tool realizations tied to the identical no-immediate-repeat repair contract; do not add fault-label-dependent or diagnostic-metric-dependent behavior.
Freeze all qualification thresholds, task set, model snapshot/config hashes, decoding, max steps, feature sets, observer family, and decision thresholds before running new episodes.
Use only the none-update baseline to determine eligible task/fault probes; apply that identical frozen probe set to all repair arms.
Do not filter probes by post-update success, failure, trajectory length, or survivorship.
Refit observers separately per repair surface after update, but keep the same observable feature family and LOSO protocol across arms.
Preserve raw traces including observations, visible admissible commands, raw model choices, pre-update selections, executed actions, update flags, fault flags, and success.
Do not use invalidated historical PF-4 results as evidence or to choose tasks, thresholds, surfaces, or faults.
Report qualification failures, insufficient fault support, budget overruns, and protocol violations as inconclusive rather than redesigning within the experiment.
